overview: In this candidate interview, Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn reviewed her first-term achievements and outlined her priorities for a potential second term. The discussion focused on city-wide infrastructure planning, social justice initiatives, and municipal restructuring to improve transparency and responsiveness.

items.title: Introduction and Personal History
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduced Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn and summarized her background as the city's youngest city councilor and her transition to the mayoralty in 2020.

items.title: Path to Politics and Early Career
items.summary: Lungo-Koehn described entering local politics due to a lack of youth and female representation and eventually running for mayor to address school safety issues and development concerns.

items.title: Parks and Public Safety Infrastructure
items.summary: The Mayor highlighted 38 ongoing park projects, including court renovations at Duggar and Playstead Parks, and noted the selection of an owner's project manager for a potential new fire headquarters.

items.title: Street Maintenance and Comprehensive Planning
items.summary: Lungo-Koehn detailed a $175 million backlog in street repairs and discussed the implementation of the city's new six-year capital improvement plan and its first comprehensive master plan.

items.title: Municipal Staffing and Department Mergers
items.summary: The Mayor explained the creation of Medford's first human resources department and the merger of offices to integrate environmental considerations into city planning and sustainability efforts.

items.title: Senior Outreach and the "Are You Okay?" Program
items.summary: Participants discussed the "Are You Okay?" program, a volunteer-led pandemic initiative that provided wellness checks and delivered essential supplies to over 11,500 local seniors.

items.title: Social Justice and Language Accessibility
items.summary: Lungo-Koehn outlined the city's social justice roadmap and her plan to use federal ARPA funding to hire a translator to improve communication with non-English speaking residents.

items.title: Coaching and Community Values
items.summary: The Mayor shared her passion for coaching youth sports and advised students to remain calm and deliberate when responding to conflict or criticism in public life.
